Rasterize an area of interest

Source: R/aoi-raster.R
rasterize_aoi.Rd

Turns an area of interest (AOI) into a raster of cells: on a template raster (such as the national 1 km template), on coarser cells that nest in the template's cells, or on a new grid at a given resolution. It is the one way constechr decides which cells an AOI gets, so tools that rasterize the same AOI with the same arguments get the same cells.

Usage

rasterize_aoi(
  aoi,
  template = NULL,
  resolution = NULL,
  crs = NULL,
  cells,
  value = "index",
  drop_na = TRUE,
  crop = TRUE
)

Arguments

aoi

The AOI: anything read_aoi() accepts (sf, sfc or SpatVector polygons, a file path, or bounds). It is read with read_aoi(aoi, crs = <target CRS>), so several polygons are dissolved into one.

template

An optional reference raster: a SpatRaster with one layer, or a path to a raster file. When given, the AOI raster aligns to it (same origin and CRS). NULL (the default) makes a new grid from the AOI and resolution.

resolution

Cell size in the units of the CRS (metres for a projected CRS such as the national template's): one positive number, or two for different x and y sizes. With a template, NULL (the default) uses the template's resolution, and any other value must be a whole multiple of it (for example 10000 on a 1000 m template), so each cell covers a block of template cells. Required without a template.

crs

The CRS of the AOI raster: anything sf::st_crs() accepts. With a template, NULL (the default) uses the template's CRS, and any other value must be the same CRS, or the function stops with an error. Without a template, NULL keeps the AOI's CRS; for bounds without a CRS (a numeric vector or a SpatExtent), crs is required and is the CRS the bounds are in.

cells

The cell inclusion rule, one of "touches" (every cell the AOI touches) or "centre" (every cell whose centre is inside the AOI). Required: there is no default, because the rule changes which cells an AOI gets. Bounds follow the same rule as polygons.

value

What the AOI's cells hold, one of:

  • "index" (the default): the cell number (terra's numbering, row by row from the top-left cell, starting at 1) in the template, or, at a coarser resolution, in the coarse grid (the template aggregated by the resolution factor). Without a template, the cell number in the new raster.

  • "template": the template's own value in each cell. Needs a template at its own resolution.

  • a single number, such as 1: that constant in every AOI cell.

drop_na

A single logical, used only with a template. TRUE (the default) drops AOI cells where the template has no data (NA), so they are NA in the result; FALSE keeps them. At a coarser resolution, a coarse cell has data if at least one of its template cells does. With value = "template", a kept cell without data holds the template's value, NA.

crop

A single logical, used only with a template. TRUE (the default) returns the cells around the AOI only; FALSE returns the template's full grid (at a coarser resolution, the full coarse grid), NA outside the AOI, as rij extraction needs.

Value

A SpatRaster with one layer, in the template's CRS (or the target CRS without a template): value in the AOI's cells and NA elsewhere. The layer is named "index" for value = "index", the template's layer name for value = "template", and "aoi" for a constant. Its extent is the AOI's bounding box snapped out to whole cells and clipped to the grid (crop = TRUE), or the full grid (crop = FALSE). Nothing is written.

Method

  • AOI: read with read_aoi() in the target CRS (the template's, or crs, or the AOI's own) and dissolved into one polygon. Reprojection, when needed, moves each vertex with PROJ (sf::st_transform()).

  • Grid with a template: the template's own cells at its resolution. At a coarser resolution, the coarse grid starts at the template's top-left corner and has ceiling(ncol / factor) columns and ceiling(nrow / factor) rows (as terra::aggregate() makes), so each coarse cell covers factor x factor template cells and coarse cells at the right and bottom edges may extend past the template.

  • Grid without a template: the AOI's bounding box with its edges snapped outwards to whole multiples of resolution (for example x 1,003,600 to 1,005,800 at 1000 m becomes 1,003,000 to 1,006,000), so rasters made separately at the same resolution and CRS line up.

  • Cropping: the grid is first cropped to the AOI's bounding box, snapped outwards to whole cells (terra::crop(), snap = "out"), and only those cells are rasterized, not the whole template.

  • Cells: raster, not vector, intersection, with terra::rasterize() (GDAL): "touches" uses touches = TRUE (GDAL's all-touched rule: every cell the AOI's boundary or interior passes through); "centre" uses touches = FALSE (cells whose centre is inside the AOI). A cell that only shares an edge with the AOI, as when bounds lie on cell boundaries, is not touched. No areas or partial cells are computed.

  • No-data cells (drop_na = TRUE, with a template): AOI cells where the template is NA are set to NA; at a coarser resolution, only coarse cells whose template cells are all NA.

  • Values: nothing is rounded, and the raster keeps the type of what it holds (ADR 0019): cell numbers are integers; the template's values are integers if the template stores integers (terra::is.int(), such as an INT* data type) and doubles if it stores floats; a constant keeps its own type (1L an integer, 1 a double). Integers outside R's integer range (possible only with INT4U or larger types) stay doubles. polygonize_raster() and terra::values() then return the same type.

  • Full grid (crop = FALSE): the result is extended to the full grid with terra::extend(), NA outside the AOI.

If the AOI's bounding box does not overlap the grid (the template, with a template), the function stops with an error. If the AOI overlaps but gets no cells (for example a small AOI that covers no cell centre, or only cells without data), it warns and returns a raster that is all NA.

See also

Other aoi: read_aoi()

Examples

template <- terra::rast(
  system.file("extdata", "template.tif", package = "constechr")
)
aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")

# On the template: each cell holds its template cell number
x <- rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, cells = "touches")
terra::values(x, mat = FALSE)
#> [1] 34 35 36 44 45 46 54 55 56

# Only cells whose centre is inside the AOI, holding 1
rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, cells = "centre", value = 1)
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 3, 3, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1003000, 1006000, 604000, 607000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> source(s)   : memory
#> varname     : template
#> name        : aoi
#> min value   :   1
#> max value   :   1

# Coarser cells (2 km on the 1 km template), numbered in the 2 km grid
rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, resolution = 2000, cells = "touches")
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 2, 2, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 2000, 2000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1002000, 1006000, 604000, 608000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> source(s)   : memory
#> name        : index
#> min value   :     7
#> max value   :    13

# The template's full grid, as rij extraction needs
rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, cells = "touches", crop = FALSE)
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 10, 10, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1000000, 1010000, 600000, 610000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> source(s)   : memory
#> varname     : template
#> name        : index
#> min value   :    34
#> max value   :    56

# Without a template: a 500 m grid from bounds
rasterize_aoi(
  c(xmin = 1003600, ymin = 604300, xmax = 1005800, ymax = 606600),
  resolution = 500,
  crs = template,
  cells = "centre"
)
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 6, 5, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 500, 500  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1003500, 1006000, 604000, 607000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> source(s)   : memory
#> name        : index
#> min value   :     6
#> max value   :    25
